threatCard.summary: A maritime security incident has significantly disrupted transit through the Strait of Hormuz, leading to a partial closure and the rerouting of vessels. This has caused a sharp increase in war-risk insurance premiums for cargo traversing the Gulf. A sustained disruption at this critical chokepoint, essential for global energy and chemical shipments, would result in lengthy reroutes and extended lead times for inbound cargo.

publicSignals.summary: Multiple wire reports describe transit through the Strait of Hormuz disrupted after a maritime security incident; several tankers are holding or rerouting and war-risk insurance premiums on Gulf-routed cargo have jumped sharply.
EIA notes a large share of seaborne crude and LNG transits the Strait of Hormuz; a sustained closure would force long reroutes and lengthen lead times for Gulf-origin energy and chemical inbound.
Shipping desks report a partial closure window at the Strait of Hormuz with carriers pausing bookings on the Gulf lane pending a security review.

playbooks.summary: Oversee the immediate and strategic response to potential disruptions from the Strait of Hormuz, focusing on all exposed suppliers to ensure continuity across critical supply chains.
steps: Convene the crisis response team promptly to assess the overall impact.
Prioritize engagement with suppliers exhibiting elevated exposure scores across all sectors.
Initiate a comprehensive review of all affected supply lanes and their material criticality.
Develop alternative sourcing strategies for crucial inputs to mitigate risk.
Communicate proactively with internal stakeholders and external partners regarding potential impacts and mitigation efforts.

playbooks.summary: Mitigate risks specific to chemical supply from the exposed region by focusing on high-impact suppliers and exploring alternative options.
steps: Contact the most exposed chemical suppliers to assess current inventory levels and transit routes.
Evaluate immediate supply chain vulnerabilities for critical chemical components.
Identify and qualify alternative sources for high-risk chemical materials.
Update inventory management plans to account for potential delays and disruptions.
Collaborate with logistics to re-route shipments if necessary.

playbooks.summary: Address potential disruptions to energy supply by engaging critical suppliers and securing diversified energy sources to ensure operational continuity.
steps: Engage with all energy suppliers identified as having exposure to the region.
Assess the direct and indirect impacts on energy commodity availability and pricing.
Develop contingency plans for energy sourcing, including alternative fuel types or suppliers.
Review and update energy consumption forecasts considering potential supply constraints.
Secure additional buffer stock of critical energy resources where feasible.

recoveryOptions.title: Expedite inbound on the most exposed lanes

recoveryOptions.title: Activate qualified backups for the dual-sourced lanes
recoveryOptions.summary: Switch the lanes that have a qualified backup on file to the alternate supplier while the primary lane is disrupted.

recoveryOptions.title: Reallocate safety stock to the highest-revenue lines
recoveryOptions.summary: Shift available on-hand cover toward the highest-revenue exposed lines to extend runway past the disruption.

recoveryOptions.title: Escalate allocation with the single-source suppliers
recoveryOptions.summary: Escalate to secure allocation from the single-source suppliers that have no qualified alternate to switch to.

supplierMessages.subject: Request for Supply Status Update - 7-Day Window
supplierMessages.body: We are conducting an impact assessment for the upcoming 7 days. Please provide an urgent update on your current shipment dates, any anticipated delays, your on-hand inventory position, and your expected recovery timeline. Additionally, please inform us if you are declaring force majeure and detail any sub-tier supplier exposure. Your prompt response is crucial for our planning.
